effect.description: one run a commit owes, written in the commit's own transaction and claimed by whichever process runs it

handler.description: the declared effect it runs, by name

target.description: the entity the committed change was about

touched.description: components moved on the target by the same commit

before.description: on a `removed` run, the component it is about as it was before the commit, by name, since the run cannot read it afterwards

kind.description: what happened to it, `matched` where a query matched it, or `started` where the target is a process that started working the effects

state.description: how far the run got — pending until a worker settles it

attempts.description: how many attempts the handler has spent; waiting through defer does not spend an attempt

generation.description: how deep in effect-written batches the commit that owed it was: 0 for a client's write, 1 for an effect's own, so what this run writes is one more

actor.description: the by/via pair that wrote the commit that owed it, so a write the run makes on that commit's behalf is signed as it was; absent for automation

error.description: what the last attempt threw — kept beside a run left failed, so the record shows why

next.description: when the run next becomes eligible after failure backoff or deferred readiness; absent means a run nobody has started or one in progress

waiting.description: the readiness condition the handler last found unmet when it deferred this run

version.description: the code version its latest attempt started on, where the host names one: resumed under another, a deploy cut the attempt off and it runs again as the same attempt; under the same one, its process crashed and that spends an attempt

lease_owner.description: the process that claimed this run

lease_token.description: that claim's token, fresh on every claim

lease_expiry.description: when the claim expires and another process may take it

lease.description: a duty held by one process at a time — its eid is derived from `name`, so two processes reaching for the same duty address one row and the winner is settled by the graph's own precondition; plumbing between the processes on one store, so it is not history

name.description: the duty being held — a sweep, a clock, a start-up pass; the eid is derived from it, so the same duty is the same row in every graph

holder.description: the process running it — absent means nobody is, and the next process to ask gets it

until.description: when the hold expires; a holder still working pushes this out on a timer, and one that was killed leaves a row that expires without anything having to clean up after it

worker.description: what a process working the effect pool says about itself, on its own process entity, every fifteen seconds while it works: how many runs it has going and the oldest of them, how many it has finished, and how busy it is. A row whose `at` stops moving is a worker that stopped saying, because it ended or its thread is stuck; one leaving the pool takes its row with it, and the next worker to start clears the row of one that was killed

running.description: how many runs it has going

runs.description: the runs it has going, oldest first, at most twenty

ran.description: how many runs it has finished since it started, however each ended

history.description: how many runs it finished in each of the last sixty whole seconds, oldest first

cpu.description: the share of one core its process used since it last said, 1 being a whole core; absent where its host cannot tell

lag.description: the longest its thread ran a timer late since it last said, in milliseconds: how full its event loop is

provisional.description: an entity whose asynchronous step has not finished yet: it sits where it always does, and the effect that finishes the step removes this mark. A reader who sees it knows the entity is not settled; the writer who started the step waits for it and never sees the mark

note.description: a line for the person reading it: why the entity is provisional, such as "saving the key"

effect_check.title: Check effect runs
effect_check.description: Check recorded background actions (effects), such as sending mail after a transaction commits. Reports runs marked failed after exhausting their attempts, runs waiting for a handler no plugin declares any more, and runs still pending past their due time by more than the server’s threshold (10 minutes by default). An overdue run can indicate that no process is running them, even while graph writes succeed. Does not retry or mark runs failed itself; with no effect records supported by the schema, reports no findings. Takes no arguments. Returns a report in content.body, with warning or failure findings when present; it does not repair the records or configuration.

effect_retry.title: Retry failed effect runs
effect_retry.description:
Put failed effect runs back to pending with a fresh attempt allowance, so the pool works them again through its ordinary path: attempts, backoff and leases as for a new run. If the cause is fixed they finish; if not they fail again and the check reports them again. Takes a handler name or a single run. Touches only failed runs of a handler some plugin declares, and says how many.

  yak effect retry send_receipt

of.description: a handler name (all its failed runs) or one run's id

effect_drop.title: Drop failed effect runs
effect_drop.description:
Delete effect runs whose work no one owes any more, so the check stops reporting them: failed runs, and pending runs whose handler no plugin declares any more. Takes a handler name or a single run, and says how many.

  yak effect drop session_run

of.description: a handler name (all its failed runs) or one run's id
